chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Rifa'ah ibn Musa, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the man who inherits land or buys it, and he pays its kharaj (land tax) to the Sultan; is there a 'ushr (tithe) upon it? He said: No.

key_terms.خَرَاج: Land tax paid to the ruling authority

ai.seo_question: Is 'ushr due on land that already pays kharaj to the government?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the principle of non-cumulative taxation by ruling that land subject to *kharaj* (land tax paid to the ruling authority) is exempt from *'ushr* (the Islamic tithe). This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between the political levy of the ruler and the religious obligation of the believer, ensuring that one form of payment does not double as the other. It serves as a foundational text for understanding the financial rights of the *Imam* versus those of the *Sultan* in classical Islamic governance.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Rifa’at Bin Musa, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘
I asked himasws about the man who inherits a land, or he buys it, and he pays its taxes to the Sultan (ruling authority), ‘Is there a tenth (10%) to pay upon it (as Zakāt)?’ Heasws said: ‘No’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from Rifa‘ah ibn Musa who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who inherits a piece of land or buys it then pays its taxes to al-Sultan (the ruler), is he required to pay one out of ten (as Zakat)?
He (the Imam) said, ‘No, he is not required to pay.’”
